rock:
Use case: photorealistic-natural.
Asset type: seamless tileable rock albedo texture for the exposed mountain faces of an existing realistic lush subtropical island in a Three.js scene.
Primary request: a photorealistic natural weathered coastal volcanic rock surface, subtle gray-brown and muted slate gray mineral tones, finely granular basalt and weathered tuff with irregular natural fractures, tiny pits, some narrow mineral veins, restrained warm mineral mottling. Convincing real geological rock rather than smooth molded plastic or artificial stripes.
Composition/framing: exactly square 2048 by 2048 pixels, orthographic straight-on close survey of one continuous solid rock surface covering every pixel edge to edge. Surface scale represents approximately 5 meters of exposed rocky cliff. Balanced mix of broad quiet rock patches, medium scale broken fracture networks, and fine granular surface detail. Crack directions vary naturally; no dominant repeating horizontal bands, no regular block or paving arrangement.
Lighting: neutral diffuse flat cross-polarized illumination suitable as PBR base color/albedo. Even exposure across the whole image, no directionally baked sunlight, no highlights, no cast shadows, no ambient occlusion painted into broad regions. Fine dark cracks are natural material color only.
Constraints: seamless opposite edges with matching continuous features for infinite tiling on both axes. Realistic moderate contrast and medium-light neutral rock, no large black crevices, no color cast. No sky, horizon, landscape composition, standalone boulders, vegetation, moss, water, soil, snow, human objects, labels, text, logos, borders, watermark. This is a production texture map, not a mountain photograph or rendered sphere.
milkyWay:
Use case: photorealistic-natural.
Asset type: full 360 by 180 degree seamless equirectangular galactic emission panorama for a realistic 3D night-sky dome. One production RGB image, exactly 2:1 landscape aspect ratio, ideally 2048 by 1024 pixels.
Primary request: photographic Milky Way diffuse light and dark dust lanes with extremely convincing fine natural structure. The galactic plane lies along the HORIZONTAL center line of the equirectangular map, running continuously across the entire image and meeting seamlessly at the left and right edges. At horizontal center the galactic bulge is a luminous but restrained warm ivory/soft taupe dense cloudy core, with natural irregular branching dark dust filaments and uneven translucent bluish-gray outer star clouds. Near the far left and right edges the same uninterrupted band is fainter and narrower. The upper and lower map regions gradually become neutral nearly black empty sky.
Composition and projection: galactic-coordinate equirectangular latitude-longitude surface map, NOT a horizon panorama. Latitude zero at the image's vertical center, galactic center longitude at the horizontal center. Milky Way band mainly confined to central 20 percent of image height, the bulge extending to at most 35 percent. The top and bottom quarters remain almost black, without a visible gradient tint. All detail at both vertical side edges matches seamlessly. No perspective, no fisheye, no curved arch.
Style: realistic neutral astronomical long-exposure nebular structure and dusty unresolved starlight; delicate filament detail and fine cloudy granular structure with natural subdued contrast, no saturated purple or orange science-fiction colors. Preserve dark gaps and branching rifts instead of a uniform glowing stripe.
Constraints: no distinct foreground star dots, no prominent bright stars or starbursts, since accurate catalogue stars will be rendered separately in 3D. Soft unresolved star-cloud grain is welcome. No constellations, connecting lines, moon, planets, comets, meteors, satellites, mountains, trees, water, buildings, horizon, captions, charts, text, logos, border, watermark. Neutral black background, not transparent. This is only the Milky Way emission layer to be added over an existing night sky; do not paint a blue sky background or terrestrial scene.
milkyWayV2:
Use case: lighting-weather.
Asset type: replacement v2 RGB emission texture for a realistic Three.js night-sky dome, a 360 x 180 degree galactic-coordinate equirectangular panorama. This is a technical texture, not a landscape.
Input image 1 is the EDIT TARGET. Keep its exact 2:1 rectangular map layout: galactic latitude zero at the horizontal centerline; galactic longitude zero / galactic center at the image center; the thin Galactic plane must continue all the way across the width and wrap seamlessly at the left and right side edges. Top and bottom quarters must stay nearly pure neutral black.
Primary edit: make this Milky Way look like delicate faint UNRESOLVED STELLAR LIGHT, instead of clouds. Replace the heavy cloudy-looking masses and bright opaque blue-gray rims with extremely fine dense pepper-like astronomical stellar grain. A very large number of tiny dim subpixel-like stars merge into a low contrast granular band, with delicate irregular interrupted dark dust lanes. The overall field should be dark, quiet, subtly visible, like the human-visible Milky Way on a dark moonless night. The central region may be only modestly brighter and slightly wider than the rest, with no bright bulging blob, no spotlight glow. Keep substantial gaps between granular star patches and let black space penetrate the band naturally.
Band mainly within the middle 15 percent of image height, extremely faint feathered unresolved starlight out to at most 26 percent at the center. Low amplitude tiny fine-grain detail should dominate, not large diffuse cloud forms. Neutral charcoal and pale warm-neutral ivory, very slight taupe variation, almost no blue. Thin broken branching dark dust filaments, no harsh edges.
Avoid: cotton-wool clouds, gray-blue atmospheric cloudbanks, massive cloudy nebulae, smoke, bright central oval, broad opaque haze, hard-edged dark cutouts, purple or orange nebula color, artificial glowing stripes, large distinct foreground stars, bright stars, diffraction spikes, starbursts, constellations, text, logos, horizon, scenery. Accurate bright catalogue stars are rendered in another layer. Do not paint a blue sky background.
Output a 2:1 equirectangular RGB map with a black background, not transparent.
